strings.name: William Ruto
strings.summary: Ruto moved from plant-science training into parliament, the agriculture ministry and the deputy presidency before becoming president in 2022. His economic agenda faces debt, tax protests and controversy over police violence. His ICC post-election-violence case ended in 2016. In 2026 he proposed tax relief and internships, requiring further legal implementation.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: As Kenyan president, influences fiscal, climate and regional-security policy and East African governance and international cooperation.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and upbringing
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Kenya’s Uasin Gishu region in 1966.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Nairobi botany and zoology BSc, 1990; plant-ecology PhD, 2018.
strings.highlights.h1.title: National leadership
strings.highlights.h1.text: Moved from deputy president to president, directing the national policy agenda.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Economic transformation
strings.highlights.h2.text: Pursues economic plans amid taxation, employment and fiscal constraints.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Tax and internship proposals
strings.timeline.t1.text: Proposed tax relief and additional 2027 internships in his Mashujaa address.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Rejects finance bill
strings.timeline.t2.text: Refused to sign the tax bill after deadly protests.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes president
strings.timeline.t3.text: Sworn in after electoral victory and Supreme Court confirmation.

strings.timeline.t5.text: The Court vacated charges and terminated the Ruto-Sang case.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Deputy president
strings.timeline.t6.text: Took office after winning election with Kenyatta.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Agriculture minister
